A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IPMF research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian convergence experiments, neural-solver benchmark results, and image-translation experiments. Only selected benchmark rows are attributed to earlier work.

after.justification: v3 retains original convergence and image-translation experiments and reports revised results using Identity initialization.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 replace independent p0-to-p0 initialization with Identity initialization, which sets x1=x0 instead of pairing independent samples. This changes the initialization procedure; the IPMF projections, solver architectures, objectives, and existing SDEdit initializations remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate high-dimensional Gaussians, Gaussian-to-Swiss-roll translation, the same SB mixture benchmark, colored MNIST 3-to-2 translation, and CelebA male-to-female translation. The initialization revisions remain within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: The compared initialization variants change: DSBM-Ind and ASBM-Ind are replaced by Identity variants in the Swiss-roll, SB benchmark, and CelebA comparisons. The corresponding IMF, IPF, IMF-OT, and SDEdit comparisons are retained, as are SF2M-Sink and the imported benchmark-best results.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported target Gaussian from N(0,Σ1) to N(3,Σ1). Figure 2 is unchanged, so this establishes a revised reported setting without establishing a rerun. Neural-solver initialization settings also change to Identity; the documented splits, metrics, architectures, and training budgets otherwise remain stable.

E4.justification: The initialization-sensitivity studies are revised to test Identity instead of independent p0-to-p0 coupling, with corresponding trajectories, translated samples, and quality/similarity curves. The SDEdit analysis and study of metrics across IPMF iterations already existed in v2; their expanded presentation is not a new analysis question.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Appendix C.7 retains the same Monte Carlo estimation procedures and sample counts.

E6.justification: Results for the independent initialization are replaced by Identity results in Table 1, the appendix BW2-UVP table, and image experiments. For example, at ε=0.1 and D=128, ASBM-Ind reports cBW2-UVP 40.32 in v2, while ASBM-Identity reports 85.2 in v3; these are different configurations, not a same-setting decline. The new CelebA tables largely summarize existing curves alongside the revised Identity results, while retained benchmark rows are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1 and 3.2, their Gaussian convergence restrictions, the continuous-time formulation in Appendix A, and the derivations and proofs in Appendix B are unchanged apart from formatting and citation presentation.

C1.justification: The abstract and new Practice II contribution explicitly claim that initialization design enables a generation-quality versus similarity tradeoff and can outperform classical initializations. This promotes an effect already discussed in v2 into a central practical contribution. The IPMF unification and Gaussian convergence claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 replaces the broad statement of comparable target-distribution fit with a solver-specific interpretation: designed couplings preserve comparable DSBM quality but sacrifice ASBM quality for similarity. Section 4.3 removes the earlier qualification about weaker results at ε=0.1. The limitation concerning unproved general convergence remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds resource links and licenses in Table 3 and hardware/training-time disclosures in Appendix C.10, including approximately five and seven A100 days per CelebA initialization for DSBM and ASBM. It removes the minibatch-permutation implementation description for the replaced independent initialization. Most existing technical details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Kim et al. on graph transformation, Ksenofontov and Korotin on categorical SB matching, Pavon et al. on data-driven SB, and Pooladian et al. on minibatch couplings. These modestly extend the context and attribution without substantially changing the relationship to IPF, IMF, DSBM, or ASBM.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, experimental motivation, and CelebA discussion receive localized revisions. Terminology, author information, and citation style also change. The overall section sequence and most explanatory and theoretical prose are retained.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two columns to one, with a redesigned title page and a horizontally rearranged Figure 1. v2 Figures 6 and 8 are consolidated into appendix Figure 7, separating FID and CMMD plots by solver. New final-metric and resource tables, revised sample panels, and restyled tables substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the practical evidence easier to assess through explicit CelebA metric tables, clearer solver-specific tradeoffs, and added resource and compute information. These are limited gains over analyses already present in v2. Reporting inconsistencies temper the improvement: Appendix C.4 groups ASBM-Identity with high-MSE cases, although Tables 2 and 5 and Figure 7 show it has the lowest MSE.
